value.definition: the name a view component carries in code

invariants.statement: A component is written where a type would be read.
The file with a component is named in lower kebab like every other file.

value.definition: the name data carries at the top of a file, outside any function

invariants.statement: Data is data whether the data is written out or built as the file loads.
A regular expression is data.
A set of fixed words is data.
A plain string is data.
A name bound to a function or to a thing the file acts on is not data wherever that name sits.

value.definition: the name a value carries inside the function working it out

invariants.statement: A name inside a function belongs to one call rather than to the file.
A parameter the body does not read opens with an underscore.

value.definition: the name a value handed to a process from outside is read under

invariants.statement: A value handed in from outside remains fixed for the whole of a run.
A name akasha reads opens with the name of the system that set that name.
A file's name is built of parts parted by dots.
Each part is a name stated elsewhere.
The first part is the slug of the page the file has or sits beside.
The part after the first part is the slug of that page's page type.
A part after those two is the file's role.
A file naming no role is the page itself.

value.definition: the part of a file's name saying what the file is to its page

invariants.statement: A role is a file property the page's type declares rather than a word chosen at the file.
A page's own file states no role.
A folder with one page is named for that page's slug.
A folder with the property pages of a page is named `properties`.
A folder with many pages of one type is named that type's plural.

value.definition: a name whose owner is outside akasha

invariants.statement: A name is its owner's where renaming the name would break a reader outside akasha.
A name its owner spells is judged by no format here.
Akasha never states that format.
That format is the owner's to change.
This name place licenses a name rather than a folder.
A name beside a name its owner spells still answers the test alone.

value.definition: the name a function carries in code

invariants.statement: A function is named for its answer rather than for how the answer is worked out.

value.definition: the address the pages of one type are reached by from outside

invariants.statement: An address is built of the page type's plural.
The plural is named elsewhere.
A listing closes with a slash.
The slash parts the listing from the page of the same name.

value.definition: the name a package is required by

invariants.statement: A package name with no scope is one slug.
A package name with a scope is that scope and a slug parted by a slash.
A scope opens with an at sign.
The at sign is the registry's mark rather than a part of either name.

value.definition: the address a page is reached by from outside

invariants.statement: An address is built of the page type's slug and the page's own.
Each slug is named elsewhere.
The page's part has a tail taken from its id.
The tail parts two pages of one slug without either page being renamed.
A part with a tail is no slug.

value.definition: the key a page has one of its values under

invariants.statement: A key is read in code.
The property the key names is called by its slug.
Lowering each capital and setting a dash before that capital gives the slug back.
The key and the slug are one name in two formats rather than two spellings.

value.definition: the name of a part of a route's path that is filled in

invariants.statement: A parameter is read in code rather than written in a path.
A parameter is named for the value that parameter has rather than for how that value is written.

value.definition: a fixed part of a route's path

invariants.statement: A segment is written as a slug is written.
A segment naming a file the route serves has that file's extension.
The part before the dot is the name.

value.definition: the name a type carries in code

invariants.statement: A type is named for the thing the type has rather than for the file the type is in.
A type and the value of the same name are parted by their case alone.
